newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian PM backs oil terminal privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian PM backs oil terminal privatisation.

text.p: Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said on Thursday that the Butinge oil terminal project had to be privatised because of the high costs involved in its construction.
"If the Lithuanian government had to finance over 50 percent of the project, it would cost the state between $150 and $200 million," Vagnorius told a news conference.
"The government cannot afford this and it does not intend to pay nearly one billion litas building an oil export terminal for Russia," he added.
Vagnorius said that about 90 percent of Butinge's business would be the export of Russian oil.
He said the government planned to hold a 34 percent stake in the terminal, which is expected to be built by late 1998. The government's stake is currently over 90 percent.
The project has had difficulty finding financing and company officials are currently negotiating with several Western banks.
